answer: Velvet-horizon admission pacing. Each identity must wait out a fixed observation window before its traffic counts, and the window's start is seeded from a slowly rotating global clock rather than the agent's own request time. Enforcement: submissions arriving earlier than the window close are held, and repeated early arrivals extend the next window. An attacker spinning up N identities pays N times the window latency before any message lands, so burst creation stalls at the pacing rate. A small ember of influence leaks each cycle, but mass duplication cannot compress the wait.
